claims.rule: Take the maximum of the amount above the upper threshold and the amount below the lower threshold.

citations.quote: Maximum of [LBSTRESN-(1.5*ULN)] and [(.5*LLN) - LBSTRESN]
Significant digits: 3
LB.LBSTNRHI
LB.LBSTNRLO
Laboratory values will be assigned a flag of abnormal (high or low) if the value is outside the threshold range (defined as significantly beyond the normal range, i.e., >1.5*ULN or <.5*LLN)
ONE = abs((LBSTRESN - (1.5 * LBSTNRHI))), TWO = abs(((.5 * LBSTNRLO) - LBSTRESN)), ALBTRVAL = ifelse(ONE > TWO, ONE, TWO),

clauses.note: Both subtraction directions are reversed in the implementation: it measures threshold minus result at the upper bound and result minus threshold at the lower bound.
The change-parameter row path uses the same reversed subtraction directions, with the raw laboratory normal limits held in helper columns.

interpretations: ULN and LLN are the source laboratory standard normal limits, as the A1HI and A1LO copy comments identify; the probe reads those raw limits through the shared source-LB lookup.
claims.assessment: The Define formula makes the signed excess beyond a threshold positive. The implementation reverses both signed differences before taking the maximum, including on change-parameter row paths. The Pilot 6 R reimplementation (adlbc.r lines 193-195) takes the absolute value of both terms and does not round; that reading is probed as ALBTRVAL__ABSOLUTE. The reimplementation builds no change-from-previous-visit parameter rows (PARAMN > 100), so it shows nothing about how those rows are filled.
claims.question: Confirm the intended signed threshold-distance formula and align the specification and retained Define comment.

probes.reading: Absolute value of each term, as the Pilot 6 R reimplementation spec/source/programs/pilot6/adlbc.r lines 193-195 compute it (ONE = abs((LBSTRESN - (1.5 * LBSTNRHI))), TWO = abs(((.5 * LBSTNRLO) - LBSTRESN)), ALBTRVAL = ifelse(ONE > TWO, ONE, TWO)); the Define formula omits the absolute values, and the program applies no rounding for the stated 3 significant digits.

If multiple assessments fall into the same visit window (windows

The appended SAP boundaries explicitly define the separate normal-range categorization: low at or below the lower normal limit, normal strictly between the limits, and high at or above the upper normal limit. The same full section subsequently defines abnormality beyond the threshold range and change from the preceding scheduled visit. These are not interchangeable ANRIND readings, and the SAP does not name ANRIND in the normal-range sentence.
claims.assessment: The citable SAP explicitly distinguishes normal-range categorization, including inclusive low/high boundaries, from threshold-range shifts and abnormal change from the preceding scheduled visit. The added normal-range boundaries do not contradict or replace the threshold-based ANRIND shift categorization. Retained ANRIND value-level ItemDefs supply the actual parameter-specific conditions, including change-parameter missingness, but the section adapter omits them; those retained rules are not classified as undocumented.

interpretations: The SAP statement about retaining post-discontinuation laboratory values and setting a washout-status flag is kept as context; it is not assumed to identify AENTMTFL or to supply an unstated washout duration.

The SAP normalizes end of treatment to Week 24 or early termination, and the guide permits a derived end-of-treatment visit; neither statement independently documents unconditional flagging of every row with that label.
The cited treatment-period definition occurs in the shift-table discussion. Its applicability to all AENTMTFL branches should be confirmed rather than silently equated with actual treatment exposure.

The appended ADSL.VISNUMEN section labels the end-of-treatment visit and literally derives it using DS records where DSTERM='PROTCOL COMPLETED'. The spelling is retained as written. It does not say that AENTMTFL uses VISNUMEN, or how a record selected under that term establishes early discontinuation of study drug.

The appended ADSL.DISCONFL section explicitly concerns discontinuation of the study and derives the flag from DCREASCD. It does not state a before-Visit-12 criterion, identify discontinuation of study drug as the same event, or link this flag to AENTMTFL. Combining DISCONFL with VISNUMEN would therefore be a proposed operational rule, not a literal documented AENTMTFL condition.
claims.assessment: Define gives a Visit 12 / early-discontinuation rule and the SAP repeatedly describes the last on-treatment observation. The specification uses a derived-row marker plus the largest eligible LBSEQ and provides no explicit Visit 12 or early-discontinuation test. The appended ADSL sections document study-discontinuation status and an end-of-treatment visit source, but do not state that their combination operationalizes AENTMTFL or resolve drug versus study discontinuation and the washout statement.
claims.question: Do the ADSL study-discontinuation flag and end-of-treatment visit define the early-discontinuation condition for AENTMTFL, and if so under which documented mapping; how are treatment-phase assessments delimited, and should last be ordered by observation date rather than LBSEQ?
claims.not_probed_reason: The literal rule requires knowing whether the subject discontinued before Visit 12 and which assessments belong to the treatment phase. The appended ADSL definitions name study-discontinuation status and the end-of-treatment visit, but do not state a dependency from AENTMTFL to DISCONFL or VISNUMEN, reconcile study with study-drug discontinuation, or supply the washout duration. Combining DISCONFL with VISNUMEN, substituting absence of a Visit 12 assessment, COMP24FL or TRTEDT alone, or reusing the scheduled-visit rank would introduce an operational condition the cited AENTMTFL rule does not state.
